subject: Post-call: Encryption & KMS options for Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Leung <sara.leung@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Encryption & KMS options for Acme Health

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps: 

Summary of requirements you mentioned:
- Data contains PII / PHI (patient identifiers, notes) — must be treated as sensitive.
- Data residency: primary storage must be within us-east-2 (Ohio) for initial roll-out.
- Data retention policy: 7 years for records; ability to configure shorter retention for non-PHI.
- Logging & audit: retain access/audit logs for 12 months; ability to forward logs to customer SIEM.
- Encryption: in-transit TLS 1.2+ required; at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys (CMEK) preferred, HSM-backed if possible.
- Key management: BYOK / customer KMS preferred; separation of keys per-tenant for production data.

Deliverables we agreed I would share:
1) High-level KMS options matrix (attached).
2) SOC 2 summary and audit artifacts pointers (attached).
3) Proposed agenda for a technical deep-dive with our SRE/Security engineer to walk through integration (Vivek suggested).

Next steps / asks:
- Sara: confirm whether FIPS 140-2 / FIPS 140-3 validated HSMs are required for the initial deployment or if FIPS is a later ramp.
- Procurement: We may need any specific PO language / contract clauses around key custody and data residency — happy to loop legal.
- Let's schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive this week or early next week.

I've attached a short KMS options matrix and our current SOC 2 summary. Vivek, looping you in to propose times and add any technical notes.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0130

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick recap and attachments — helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- HSM / FIPS: For PHI storage we prefer HSM-backed keys with FIPS 140-2 or 140-3 validation. If you support non-FIPS options initially, we can evaluate a phased approach, but procurement will prefer FIPS-certified.
- Key rotation / separation: We need per-tenant key separation (no shared root key across customers) and automated rotation policies (at least annual rotation). Can your solution support customer-specific rotation schedules?
- Logging redaction: For logs that may include user-generated content, we need token-level redaction or redaction hooks prior to persistence.
- Audit evidence: procurement will need a short list of audit artifacts (SOC 2 controls mapping to encryption + access controls) to attach to the SOW.

We can do a deep-dive on Wed 6/23 10am ET or Thu 6/24 2pm ET. Which works for your team?

-Sara Leung
Head of Security Operations
Acme Health
+sara.leung@acmehealth.com

Hi Sara,

Appreciate the clarifications. Short answers here, and we'll cover details in the deep-dive. I've also attached a short technical note.

- FIPS / HSM: We support CMEK integrations with AWS KMS (including CloudHSM-backed keys), Google Cloud KMS (Cloud HSM), and Azure Key Vault (HSM-backed). For our hosted offering we can integrate customer-managed keys in a FIPS-backed KMS. If you require an on-premises HSM integration, we support KMIP / PKCS#11 integrations for our Private deployments.
- Per-tenant separation & rotation: We offer per-customer key isolation for Dedicated and Private deployments. Rotation policies can be configured and automated; we also support manual rotation workflows where required.
- Logging & redaction: We offer token-level redaction hooks in the ingest layer (tokens can be redacted before persistent logs). Audit/audit-log retention is configurable and can be forwarded to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog/Elastic).
- Audit artifacts: SOC 2 mapping and a controls checklist are included in the SOC summary; Dev will follow up with any additional evidence we can share under NDA.

Next steps:
1) Schedule technical deep-dive: Vivek / Dev / Marissa (Redwood) + Sara / Acme Security. Proposed slots: Wed 2027-06-23 10:00 ET or Thu 2027-06-24 14:00 ET. Please confirm.
2) I'll open a HubSpot MAP and share an initial SOW template and the requested audit checklist.
3) If Acme procurement prefers an NDA before evidence exchange, I can send a standard Redwood mutual NDA.

Attached: kms-technical-note.pdf (3 pages).

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: kms-technical-note.pdf

Hi Sara / Marissa,

Thanks — quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive: 

Encryption in transit:
- We enforce TLS 1.3 (fallback to TLS 1.2 where legacy clients require). Mutual TLS is supported for backend service-to-service communication; customer gateways can require mTLS for additional assurance.

Encryption at rest:
- Data is encrypted using AES-256-GCM. Keys are stored in customer-managed KMS when CMEK is enabled; otherwise we use per-tenant service keys.
- For hosted (multi-tenant) customers we offer envelope encryption with customer master keys stored in the customer's cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure KV).

KMS / HSM integration options:
- AWS: KMS + CloudHSM (FIPS certified) integration supported; keys can be imported or generated in CloudHSM.
- GCP: Cloud KMS with Cloud HSM-backed keys.
- Azure: Key Vault Managed HSM options available.
- Private deployments: we support KMIP and PKCS#11 to integrate with on-prem HSMs (Thales, Gemalto, YubiHSM).
- Key rotation & caching: short-lived data encryption keys (DEKs) are cached at the serving layer to avoid latency hits on every token issuance; master key operations (wrap/unwrap) occur less frequently. We can document rotation windows and cache TTLs in the deep-dive.

Audit & logging:
- Access and control plane actions are logged and can be retained for configurable windows; logs can be redacted at ingest and forwarded to customer SIEMs.
- We can provide an ops-runbook describing evidence types (KMS audit logs, access logs, config snapshots) for procurement.

Potential impacts / trade-offs to discuss:
- Latency: integrating on every token call to an HSM is impractical; we use envelope encryption + caching to balance security and latency.
- Private vs Hosted: Dedicated/Private deployments give stronger isolation and allow configuring HSMs directly in-customer-network.

Proposed deep-dive agenda (45-60 min):
1) Walk through Acme requirements (Sara) — 10 min
2) KMS/HSM options & recommended architecture for us-east-2 — 15 min
3) Logging / redaction / retention approach — 10 min
4) Q&A and action items (NDA, evidence list, timeline) — 10-15 min

I'll prepare a short deck showing the envelope encryption flow and expected latency numbers. Please confirm the meeting slot and any additional attendees from your side.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Architect — Security
Redwood Inference
